# @rootnative/web

> A standalone web runtime for React Native apps. The app imports
> react-native, the Vite plugin resolves that name to @rootnative/web, and the
> app runs in the browser as a real web app: semantic HTML, atomic CSS, server
> rendering, and SEO tags. It doesn't use react-native-web.

Status: early alpha. The API can change between releases. Every component and
API has tests that run in real browsers: Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit, the
engine of Safari.

Docs: https://rootnative.github.io/web/
Full: https://rootnative.github.io/web/llms-full.txt
Source: https://github.com/rootnative/web

## Install

npm install @rootnative/web

Peers: react ^19.0.0, react-dom ^19.0.0. ESM only.

1. Add the Vite plugin (Vite 8) to vite.config.ts:
   import { rootnative } from '@rootnative/web/vite'
   plugins: [react(), rootnative()]
   With Reanimated, or a library built on it: rootnative({ worklets: true }).
   It runs the Babel plugin of react-native-worklets on the app code and the
   libraries. The app needs react-native-worklets and @babel/core.
   It resolves react-native to @rootnative/web (the exact name only), resolves
   .web.* files first, defines __DEV__ (true on the dev server, false in a
   production build, from NODE_ENV), and puts 'web' in place of Platform.OS.
   It also defines global as globalThis, resolves
   @react-native/assets-registry/registry to @rootnative/web/assets-registry,
   resolves the two react-native-web style files that Reanimated 4 imports to
   @rootnative/web/style, and gives pre-bundled dependencies the .web.*
   extensions.
   An alias or a __DEV__ define in your own config wins.
2. Add src/react-native.d.ts (in a folder that tsconfig.json includes):
   declare module 'react-native' { export * from '@rootnative/web' }
   The file must have no top-level import or export line. With one,
   TypeScript reports "Cannot find module 'react-native'". Don't map the name
   with tsconfig "paths": the package has no main or types field. The file
   also gives the type of __DEV__. For .web.tsx files, add
   "moduleSuffixes": [".web", ""] to tsconfig.json.
3. Give the page a full-height flex root:
   html, body, #root { height: 100%; margin: 0 }
   #root { display: flex; flex-direction: column }
   Then createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(<App />).
   flex: 1 on the root View fills the window, as on iOS and Android.

Browsers: Chrome 95, Edge 95, Firefox 93, Safari 15.1, iOS Safari 15.1.

Without the plugin (another bundler): alias the exact name react-native to
@rootnative/web, put a .web variant of each extension first, and define
__DEV__ and global (as globalThis). In Vite, set the defines in define and in
optimizeDeps.rolldownOptions.transform.define, and the extensions in
resolve.extensions and optimizeDeps.rolldownOptions.resolve.extensions: the
dependency optimizer has its own. Add the compat aliases that a library
needs. Platform.OS then stays a read at run time.

Server rendering with Vite: the plugin applies to app code on the server. A
dependency that Vite leaves to Node gets no __DEV__ and throws a
ReferenceError. Add it to ssr.noExternal.

## Entry points

- @rootnative/web: the React Native components and APIs. Import it as
  react-native through the plugin.
- @rootnative/web/dom: web-only features. Head.
- @rootnative/web/server: createStyleRegistry, StyleRegistryProvider,
  renderStyleTags, styleTagsHTML, StyleRegistry.
- @rootnative/web/vite: rootnative(), the Vite plugin. Only in vite.config.ts.

Import /dom and /server only in code that runs on the web.

## What ships

Components: View, Text, Image, Pressable, TouchableHighlight,
TouchableNativeFeedback, TouchableOpacity, TouchableWithoutFeedback, Button,
ScrollView, FlatList, RefreshControl, TextInput, Switch, ActivityIndicator,
Modal, KeyboardAvoidingView, StatusBar.

APIs: StyleSheet, Platform, Dimensions, useWindowDimensions, Appearance,
useColorScheme, AppState, Keyboard, Linking, Alert, Share, Vibration, Clipboard,
AccessibilityInfo, I18nManager, BackHandler, PixelRatio, processColor,
PanResponder, usePressability.

Compat, for libraries only, do not call in app code: unstable_createElement,
findNodeHandle, TurboModuleRegistry.

NOT IMPLEMENTED, do not import:
- SectionList, VirtualizedList, Animated, LayoutAnimation.
- A Next.js plugin, and templates for a Vite app with and without server
  rendering.

Out of scope: Expo, Metro, React 18, CommonJS, Flow.

A component ref is the DOM element, typed HostInstance (ViewInstance,
TextInstance, ImageInstance, PressableInstance). It has measure(callback),
measureInWindow(callback), measureLayout(ancestor, onSuccess, onFail), and
setNativeProps({ style }). Each one calls its callback at once, with CSS
pixels from getBoundingClientRect(). The window is the visible area.
setNativeProps writes an inline style, and any other prop has no effect.
Type a ref as useRef<ViewInstance>(null), not useRef<HTMLElement>(null).
ScrollView, FlatList, and TextInput add the methods listed below.

## Semantic HTML

The role prop picks the element:
- article, figure, form, main: the element of the same name.
- banner: header. complementary: aside. contentinfo: footer.
  navigation: nav. list: ul. listitem: li.
- button: <button type="button">, so it never submits a form.
- heading: h1 to h6 from aria-level. The default level is 2.
- link with href: a.
- separator: hr. With children: a div with the role.
- Any other role, and the table roles: the default element (div for View,
  span for Text) with a role attribute.

href on a View or a Text renders an <a> (web only). On Text, target, rel,
download, and lang pass to the element (web only).

accessibilityRole works. role wins when both are set. Old names map: header to
heading, image to img, imagebutton to button, summary to region, adjustable to
slider, search to searchbox, text and keyboardkey to none.

Accessibility props become ARIA attributes: accessibilityLabel is aria-label,
accessibilityHint is aria-description, accessibilityLiveRegion is aria-live,
accessibilityState and accessibilityValue are aria-* states,
accessibilityViewIsModal is aria-modal, accessibilityElementsHidden is
aria-hidden. nativeID is id. testID is data-testid. focusable is tabIndex 0,
or -1 for false. tabIndex wins.

aria-* and data-* props pass through. An aria-* prop wins over the mapped
prop. DOM event handlers (onClick, onKeyDown, ...) pass to the element (web
only). Any other prop that isn't a React Native prop is dropped.

## Styles

- StyleSheet.create freezes the objects, and a frozen style compiles to atomic
  CSS once. An inline style object compiles again on each render.
- View defaults: display flex, flexDirection column, alignItems stretch,
  flexShrink 0, position relative, border box. Text defaults: 14 px, black,
  system font, spaces and line breaks kept.
- Numbers get px, lineHeight too. flex, flexGrow, flexShrink, opacity, zIndex,
  aspectRatio, and fontWeight stay unitless. Strings pass through.
- Colors use the React Native parser. A color it can't parse is dropped.
- flex: 1 is 1 1 0%. flex: 0 is 0 0 auto. flex: -1 is 0 1 auto.
- Any style wins over a default (flex: 1 beats the default flexShrink 0). A
  longhand wins over a shorthand, whatever the key order.
- Start and end props (marginStart, paddingEnd, start, end, borderStartWidth,
  borderTopStartRadius, ...) become logical CSS and flip in right-to-left.
- marginLeft, paddingLeft, left, and their right partners stay physical in a
  right-to-left layout. Native swaps them by default. Use start and end props
  for anything that must follow the direction.
- transform, boxShadow, and filter take the React Native array or a CSS
  string. shadow* props become box-shadow when boxShadow isn't set.
  textShadow* props become text-shadow.
- fontFamily 'System' is the browser's system font stack. Named font weights
  become numbers.
- elevation, borderCurve, includeFontPadding, overlayColor: no web effect.
- Types: the style props take React Native 0.88's ViewStyle, TextStyle, and
  ImageStyle, and StyleSheet.create checks each key and value. touchAction is
  the one web-only key. transform takes no Animated value, and resizeMode has
  no 'none' yet. Any other CSS property passes through at runtime but needs a
  cast: { transition: '...' } as ViewStyle, or as unknown as ViewStyle for a
  value that React Native's type doesn't allow.

## Components

View
- onLayout comes from a ResizeObserver. It fires after mount and after each
  size change. A move with no size change doesn't fire it.
- pointerEvents: none, auto, box-none, box-only.

Text
- numberOfLines 1 ends the line with an ellipsis. A larger number clamps.
- ellipsizeMode: tail and clip. head and middle show the ellipsis at the end.
- selectable is true by default on the web (false on native).
- onPress, onPressIn, onPressOut, onLongPress, and pressRetentionOffset work
  as on Pressable. The event is a GestureResponderEvent. As on native, only
  onPress or onLongPress makes a Text pressable. suppressHighlighting is
  ignored, as on Android.
- A pressable Text with no role has role="link", is in the tab order, and
  Enter or Space presses it. With href it renders an <a>. role="button"
  renders a <button>. disabled sets aria-disabled, and the Text isn't
  pressable, so a pressable parent gets the press.
- On a pressable Text, onClick and the other DOM handlers run before the press
  handlers, and both run.

Image
- Renders a div box with an <img> inside. The style sizes the box. With no
  size in the style or the source, it's 0 x 0, as on native.
- source: { uri }; an array with scale (srcset x) or width (srcset w);
  { uri, headers } with method and body (loads with fetch); a URL string from
  a bundler import (web only). A number from require() loads nothing and
  warns once.
- resizeMode: cover (default), contain, stretch, center, repeat.
- tintColor, blurRadius, defaultSource work. onProgress never fires.
- loading, fetchPriority, decoding: web only, passed to the <img>.
- Statics: getSize (rejects on the server), getSizeWithHeaders, prefetch
  (resolves true), queryCache (resolves {}), resolveAssetSource (null for a
  number).

Pressable
- role="button" renders <button type="button">. Without a role, a focusable
  div. Give an action role="button".
- style and children can be functions of { pressed, hovered, focused }.
  hovered (web only) is a mouse or pen, never touch. focused (web only) is
  keyboard focus.
- Mouse, pen, touch: primary button only. Keyboard: Enter or Space.
- onLongPress after delayLongPress, 500 ms by default. A press shows at least
  130 ms, as on native.
- onPress gets the pointer up event, or the click event for a keyboard or
  assistive technology press. preventDefault() on it cancels the click.
- The click that follows a tap stops when it lands outside the pressed
  element, for example on a modal that the press opened. A click on the
  pressed element goes through.
- hitSlop grows the hit area with a ::before box. A parent with overflow
  hidden clips it.
- pressRetentionOffset defaults to 20 on three sides and 30 at the bottom.
- cancelable={false} sets touch-action: none.
- disabled sets aria-disabled, leaves the tab order, and stops every press.
- android_ripple, android_disableSound, blockNativeResponder: ignored.

TouchableHighlight
- The press handling of Pressable, with no minimum press duration. A div
  around one child that takes a style. role="button" renders a button.
- While pressed: underlayColor (default black) as the background, and
  activeOpacity (default 0.85) on the child. After onPress, the underlay
  stays for delayPressOut ms, so a short tap shows it. No press handler, no
  underlay. testOnly_pressed shows it. onShowUnderlay, onHideUnderlay.
- Give the child an opaque background color, or the underlay shows at full
  strength.
- In the tab order only with onPress. onFocus and onBlur fire.
  rejectResponderTermination sets touch-action: none.

TouchableNativeFeedback
- Works as TouchableWithoutFeedback, with no ripple, as on iOS. background
  and useForeground are ignored.
- SelectableBackground(), SelectableBackgroundBorderless(), and Ripple(color,
  borderless, rippleRadius) return the objects of React Native.
  canUseNativeForeground() is false. Call Ripple outside a component: the
  React Compiler lint reads a capitalized call as a component.

TouchableOpacity
- The press handling of Pressable, with no minimum press duration.
  role="button" renders <button type="button">. Without a role, a div.
- Dims to activeOpacity (default 0.2) at once when a press starts, and over
  150 ms when the pointer comes back into the press area. Fades back to the
  style's opacity over 250 ms when the press ends or the pointer leaves, and
  when disabled or the style's opacity changes. Easing.inOut(Easing.quad),
  through the Web Animations API, with no new render.
- In the tab order only with onPress, as on native. onFocus and onBlur fire
  (native doesn't call them). rejectResponderTermination sets touch-action:
  none. hitSlop and pressRetentionOffset as on Pressable.
- touchSoundDisabled, hasTVPreferredFocus, nextFocus*: ignored.

TouchableWithoutFeedback
- No element of its own. Its only child gets the press handlers (the child's
  own DOM handlers run first), the accessibility props, role, testID,
  nativeID, id, and onLayout. style stays out, as on native.
- onFocus and onBlur replace the child's. Without them, the child keeps its
  own. The child is in the tab order only with onPress and not disabled.
- hitSlop goes to the child, but a View doesn't grow its hit area yet.
  rejectResponderTermination is ignored.

Button
- <button type="button"> with the title in a Text, on TouchableOpacity: it
  dims to 0.2 while pressed. title must be a string, or Button throws.
- The look of the Android button: background #2196F3, white text, weight 500,
  radius 2, 8 px around the title. color sets the background. The title keeps
  its case (Android makes it uppercase). No elevation.
- disabled (or aria-disabled, or accessibilityState.disabled): background
  #dfdfdf, text #a1a1a1, aria-disabled, out of the tab order, no press.
- Takes only the props of React Native's Button: no style, no children. For
  another look, use Pressable with role="button".
- accessibilityLanguage sets lang. accessibilityActions,
  onAccessibilityAction, touchSoundDisabled, hasTVPreferredFocus, nextFocus*:
  ignored. Ref: the button element.

ScrollView
- Scrolls its own box, not the document. On a phone, the browser's address
  bar doesn't hide as it scrolls.
- onScroll: one event per frame. nativeEvent has contentOffset, contentSize,
  layoutMeasurement. No velocity. scrollEventThrottle isn't needed.
- A scroll while a pointer is down is a drag. A scroll after the release, or
  with no pointer (wheel, keyboard, scrollTo), is momentum. The scroll ends at
  scrollend, or 150 ms after the last scroll event.
- scrollEnabled={false} hides the overflow.
- snapToInterval, snapToOffsets, pagingEnabled snap after the scroll settles.
- stickyHeaderIndices: vertical only. keyboardDismissMode: on-drag works.
- refreshControl wraps the scroller and gets the style props that place the
  box (margins, flex, sizes, position, transform, gaps), as on Android. The
  scroller fills it and keeps the rest of the style.
- Ref: the scroll element plus scrollTo({ x, y, animated }) (animated defaults
  to true), scrollToEnd({ animated }), getScrollableNode(),
  getInnerViewNode(). flashScrollIndicators() does nothing.
- scrollTo(y, x), the old positional form, doesn't work: the DOM
  scrollTo(x, y) takes the arguments in the other order.
- Native-only props (bounces, decelerationRate, contentInset, the zoom props,
  ...) are ignored.

RefreshControl
- Pass it to ScrollView as refreshControl, or give FlatList onRefresh and
  refreshing. Pull to refresh with TOUCH ONLY: mouse, pen, and keyboard have
  no pull, so add a refresh button too.
- A pull starts at the top of the list when the finger first moves down. The
  indicator moves half the finger distance. A release after 128 px of finger
  calls onRefresh. onRefresh must set refreshing to true at once, or the
  indicator goes back. No pull while refreshing or with enabled={false}.
- In a flipped scroller (an inverted FlatList), the indicator sits at the
  bottom and the pull goes up, as on native.
- Android's look: an arc on a white disc (40 px, size="large" 56 px), at rest
  64 px under progressViewOffset minus the disc. colors[0], else tintColor,
  else black, is the arc. progressBackgroundColor is the disc.
- title is the accessible name; no visible text. titleColor: no effect.
- View props and the ref go to the wrapper, which has aria-busy.

FlatList
- NO VIRTUALIZER. It renders every item. Load a long list in pages with
  onEndReached.
- Ignored: initialNumToRender, maxToRenderPerBatch, windowSize,
  updateCellsBatchingPeriod, removeClippedSubviews, disableVirtualization,
  extraData, getItemLayout.
- Works as on native: data, renderItem, keyExtractor, ItemSeparatorComponent,
  ListHeaderComponent, ListFooterComponent, ListEmptyComponent, numColumns,
  columnWrapperStyle, horizontal, inverted, initialScrollIndex,
  onViewableItemsChanged, viewabilityConfig, viewabilityConfigCallbackPairs,
  onStartReached, CellRendererComponent, renderScrollComponent,
  stickyHeaderIndices, and the ScrollView props.
- onEndReached fires once per content length. The default threshold is 2 px.
  A list shorter than its viewport fires it after mount.
- onRefresh and refreshing wrap the scroller in a RefreshControl, with
  progressViewOffset, as on native. With onRefresh, refreshing must be a
  boolean, or the list throws. A refreshControl prop wins.
  renderScrollComponent gets the three props and adds its own control.
- Ref: scrollToOffset, scrollToIndex (a row index with numColumns),
  scrollToItem, scrollToEnd, recordInteraction, getScrollableNode.
  onScrollToIndexFailed never fires.

TextInput
- An <input type="text">, or a <textarea> with multiline. No border, padding,
  or background, as on iOS.
- multiline grows with the text. numberOfLines is the minimum row count.
- Enter in a single-line field calls onSubmitEditing, then blurs. Inside a
  <form>, the form submits too. In a multiline field, Enter adds a line unless
  submitBehavior is submit or blurAndSubmit. Shift+Enter always adds a line.
- keyboardType becomes inputmode, and the type stays text, so the browser adds
  no validation. returnKeyType becomes enterkeyhint. secureTextEntry is
  type="password". showSoftInputOnFocus={false} is inputmode="none".
- editable={false} is readonly, not disabled.
- autoComplete and textContentType use the HTML tokens. React Native-only
  values map (name-given to given-name, sms-otp to one-time-code).
- A value with no change handler stays fixed, with no React warning.
- Ref: the element plus clear(), isFocused(), getNativeRef(),
  setNativeProps({ text, style }). TextInput.State has currentlyFocusedInput(),
  focusTextInput(element), blurTextInput(element).

Switch
- <input type="checkbox" role="switch">, transparent, over a drawn track and
  thumb. The browser gives the press, Space, the focus, and <label for>.
- Controlled, as on native: it shows value (only true is on). A press calls
  onChange (nativeEvent.value, nativeEvent.target), then onValueChange(value).
  When value doesn't change, the switch goes back.
- The look of the Android switch: 40 by 20 px, track #939393 off and #A3D3CF
  on, thumb #FAFAFA off and #009688 on. trackColor={{ false, true }} and
  thumbColor replace them. The thumb moves over 150 ms, not with
  prefers-reduced-motion. Right-to-left puts the on position at the left.
- disabled (or accessibilityState.disabled): the input is disabled, and the
  switch has an opacity of 0.5.
- style, onLayout, and pointerEvents go to the root element, which has
  alignSelf: flex-start. A width and height in style change the size. The
  ref, id, testID, and the accessibility props go to the input.
- ios_backgroundColor, onTintColor, tintColor, thumbTintColor: ignored.

ActivityIndicator
- A spinner: an SVG that turns once each 0.75 s, in an element with
  role="progressbar". size: small (20 px, the default), large (36 px), or a
  number. color: the default is #999999.
- animating={false} stops and hides it, and it keeps its space.
  hidesWhenStopped={false} keeps a stopped indicator visible.
- Two elements, as on native: style and onLayout go to a container that
  centers the indicator. The ref and the other props go to the indicator.
- It turns also with prefers-reduced-motion.

Modal
- A <dialog> opened with showModal(), in a portal on <body>: the top layer,
  above every zIndex. The rest of the page is inert and doesn't scroll.
- visible decides (default true). Escape, and the back gesture of Chrome on
  Android, call onRequestClose: hide the modal there. While visible is true,
  the modal stays open.
- onShow fires once per show, when the enter animation ends. onDismiss fires
  after visible becomes false and the exit animation ends, not on unmount.
- The focus moves into the modal (the first control, or the dialog itself),
  and back to the opener when it hides.
- A press inside doesn't reach a Pressable around the Modal. A nested modal
  goes on top, and Escape closes the top one first.
- The children go in a box that fills the viewport: white, backdropColor, or
  clear with transparent. style goes to the box. ref and modalRef are the
  <dialog>. testID, aria props, and DOM handlers go to the <dialog>.
- Renders nothing on the server. It shows after hydration.
- animationType: slide (up from the bottom) or fade, 200 ms with the curves
  of the Android modal; none (default) is instant. The modal stays until its
  exit animation ends and takes no presses then; a nested modal closes at
  once. Reduced motion: instant.
- presentationStyle, supportedOrientations, onOrientationChange,
  allowSwipeDismissal, hardwareAccelerated, statusBarTranslucent,
  navigationBarTranslucent: ignored.
- Firefox before 98 and Safari before 15.4 have no showModal(): a fixed box
  on top, Escape works, the page isn't inert.

StatusBar
- backgroundColor writes <meta name="theme-color"> in the browser, after
  mount, so the server HTML doesn't have it. The last mounted StatusBar wins.
- barStyle, hidden, translucent: no web effect. StatusBar.currentHeight is
  null.
- Head themeColor writes the same tag. Use one of the two.

## APIs

- Platform: OS is 'web'. select() uses web, then default. A native key
  doesn't apply. Version is the user agent ('' on the server).
  constants.reactNativeVersion is 0.88.1. isTV is false. isTesting is true when
  NODE_ENV is test. isDisableAnimations follows prefers-reduced-motion. The
  Vite plugin puts 'web' in place of each Platform.OS read at build time.
  Platform.select keeps its code.
- StyleSheet: create, flatten, compose, absoluteFill, absoluteFillObject.
  hairlineWidth is 1.
- Dimensions: window is innerWidth and innerHeight. screen is the display.
  scale is devicePixelRatio. fontScale is the root font size divided by 16.
  get('window' | 'screen'). addEventListener('change', fn) returns
  { remove() }.
- Appearance: getColorScheme() returns the override, else
  prefers-color-scheme. setColorScheme('light' | 'dark') overrides it for the
  app and sets color-scheme on <html>. null or 'unspecified' clears it.
  addChangeListener(fn) returns { remove() }.
- AppState: currentState is 'active' while the page is visible, else
  'background' ('active' on the server). No 'inactive'. addEventListener:
  'change' (visibilitychange, and 'background' on pagehide), 'blur' and
  'focus' (the browser window, as on Android), 'memoryWarning' (never fires).
  Returns { remove() }. An unknown event throws.
- Linking: openURL opens a URL of this site in this tab, a URL of another
  site in a new tab (no opener; rejects when the browser blocks it, so call
  it from a press handler), and mailto:, tel:, sms:, and other schemes from
  this tab. javascript: and data: reject. A URL that isn't a string or is
  empty throws at once. canOpenURL is true for each URL that openURL tries.
  getInitialURL is the URL that the page loaded with (null on the server).
  The 'url' event NEVER fires on the web: the router owns the URL. emit,
  addListener, removeAllListeners, listenerCount work. openSettings rejects.
  sendIntent rejects with 'Unsupported'. For a link that the user clicks,
  prefer href on Text or View.
- Alert.alert(title, message?, buttons?, options?): a <dialog
  role="alertdialog"> with showModal(), outside the React tree, with the look
  of Android's alert (teal text buttons; dark gray card in the dark scheme,
  from Appearance or userInterfaceStyle). All buttons show, in order; with
  three, the first sits at the start. No buttons or [] give OK. A press closes
  the alert, then calls onPress(). style 'destructive' is red text. Focus:
  isPreferred, else the cancel button, else the first.
- Alert: Escape (and Chrome's Android back gesture) presses the style
  'cancel' button. Without one, Escape and a click outside close the alert
  only with cancelable: true, then onDismiss runs. A new alert goes on top.
  Alert.prompt does nothing yet (dev warning). On the server, nothing.
- Keyboard: as on Android. keyboardDidShow fires when the on-screen keyboard
  shows and when its height changes, keyboardDidHide when it hides. The Will
  and ChangeFrame events never fire. The keyboard comes from the visual
  viewport, which shrinks by it, and counts only while a text field has the
  focus; with navigator.virtualKeyboard.overlaysContent, from its rectangle.
  Events: duration 0, easing 'keyboard', endCoordinates in CSS px (screenY =
  top of the keyboard from the window top). dismiss() blurs the focused text
  field. isVisible(), metrics(). scheduleLayoutAnimation does nothing. No
  event on a desktop or with a hardware keyboard.
- KeyboardAvoidingView: React Native 0.88 math. behavior 'padding'
  (paddingBottom), 'height' (first height less the covered part, flex: 0),
  'position' (inner view with contentContainerStyle, moved by bottom), none
  (plain View). The frame comes from onLayout, so y is relative to the
  parent: pass the distance to the window top in keyboardVerticalOffset, as on
  native. No animation.
- Share: share({ title, message, url }) calls navigator.share with title,
  text (the message), and url. Resolves { action: 'sharedAction' |
  'dismissedAction', activityType: null }; a closed sheet is dismissedAction.
  REJECTS with 'Unsupported platform' where the browser has no share sheet
  (for example Firefox on a desktop, or a page on plain http). Call it from a press handler. options
  have no effect.
- Vibration: navigator.vibrate with Android's rules. A number is
  milliseconds (default 400). An array is [wait, vibrate, wait, ...]. repeat
  plays an array again until cancel(). Does nothing where the browser has no
  Vibration API (Safari, iOS, most desktops).
- Clipboard (deprecated in React Native): setString writes with
  navigator.clipboard.writeText, or a hidden textarea and
  execCommand('copy') on a page with no Clipboard API. A refused write only
  warns in development. getString reads with readText and REJECTS when the
  browser refuses. Call both from a press handler.
- AccessibilityInfo: reduce motion, reduce transparency, invert colors, and
  high contrast read live media queries, with change events.
  isScreenReaderEnabled, isAccessibilityServiceEnabled, isBoldTextEnabled, and
  isGrayscaleEnabled are ALWAYS false on the web. Don't gate a feature on them.
  announceForAccessibility writes to an aria-live="polite" region;
  announceForAccessibilityWithOptions with { queue: false } uses assertive.
  setAccessibilityFocus takes the element, not a node handle. Give a View
  tabIndex={-1} so that it can take focus.
- I18nManager: isRTL reads the dir of <html> each time. forceRTL sets dir on
  <html> at once. allowRTL(false) changes only what isRTL reports.
  swapLeftAndRightInRTL stores the flag and has no effect on styles. isRTL is
  false on the server.
- BackHandler: listeners register and never fire. exitApp() does nothing. Use
  the history API of your router.
- PixelRatio: get() is devicePixelRatio. getFontScale() is the root font size
  divided by 16. Both are 1 on the server. getPixelSizeForLayoutSize and
  roundToNearestPixel work.
- processColor: an unsigned 32-bit ARGB integer, as on iOS. null for a color
  it can't parse.
- PanResponder: runs on pointer events. panHandlers are six pointer handlers;
  spread them on a View. Set touchAction: 'none' in the style (or 'pan-y' for
  a horizontal drag in a vertical scroll), or the browser scrolls instead.
  The element captures the pointer at the grant. Negotiation works as on
  native. dx and dy are CSS pixels; vx and vy are pixels per millisecond.
  onShouldBlockNativeResponder is ignored. getInteractionHandle() is null.
- usePressability(config): returns pointer, keyboard, and focus handlers, not
  the native responder handlers. Spread them on a View. Memoize the config.
  A null config returns null. hitSlop doesn't grow the hit area. Set
  touchAction yourself for cancelable={false}.
- unstable_createElement(type, props): compat, not in React Native. Renders an
  element from React Native props: style compiles to class names, the
  accessibility props become ARIA attributes, onPress and the responder
  handlers are dropped, every other prop goes to the element. No style reset.
- findNodeHandle(value): compat. Returns the DOM element of a ref, of an
  element, or of a ScrollView ref. A number comes back as it is. null for a
  class component instance.
- TurboModuleRegistry: compat. get() returns null, getEnforcing() throws.
- @rootnative/web/assets-registry: compat entry with registerAsset and
  getAssetByID. The Vite plugin aliases @react-native/assets-registry/registry
  to it. Empty unless your code registers an asset.
- @rootnative/web/style: compat entry for Reanimated 4. createReactDOMStyle
  (also the default export) gives inline DOM style values, shorthands first.
  createTransformValue and createTextShadowValue give CSS values. Without the
  Worklets Babel plugin, pass the shared values as a dependency array to each
  Reanimated hook.

## Server rendering

Render the whole <html> document with React, not only the app:

  const registry = createStyleRegistry()
  const html = renderToString(
    <html lang="en">
      <head>...</head>
      <body>
        <div id="root">
          <StyleRegistryProvider registry={registry}><App /></StyleRegistryProvider>
        </div>
        <script type="module" src="/client.js" />
      </body>
    </html>,
  )
  const page = `<!doctype html>${html.replace('</head>', `${styleTagsHTML(registry)}</head>`)}`

- One registry per request.
- Write the style tags after the render ends.
- Render <head> with React, so the tags of Head land in it. Pasted into a
  template, they land at the start of <body>.
- renderStyleTags(registry) returns the same three <style> elements as React
  elements.
- The client calls hydrateRoot(root, <App />) with no provider. It adopts the
  server's <style> elements, so it inserts no rule twice.

On the server and during hydration, useWindowDimensions() returns
{ width: 0, height: 0, scale: 1, fontScale: 1 } and useColorScheme() returns
'light'. The real values arrive after hydration. Dimensions.get() and
Appearance.getColorScheme() return the real value in the browser at once, so
don't read them in render: the first render won't match the server HTML.

## Head

import { Head } from '@rootnative/web/dom'

Props: title, description, canonical, robots, themeColor, openGraph (title,
description, image, url, type, siteName), jsonLd (one schema.org object or an
array), children (extra meta, link, and title elements).

- Use one Head per page. React doesn't merge two.
- Its tags go away when it unmounts.
- The JSON-LD script stays in the body. A < in the data is escaped.
